transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-31 10:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Quantaco Head of ML), Markus (Infra Lead), Priya (Finance), Avery (Product)
Links mentioned: cost spreadsheet (redwood.com/fire/redwood-costs.xlsx), pilot runbook (doc link), benchmark results (shared during call)

Summary: quick review of last week's benchmark, focused on tokens/sec/$ numbers, caching wins, and batching vs latency tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share full spreadsheet, SE to run tuning experiments, Quantaco to provide traces, schedule security follow-up.

Transcript: 
00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining our weekly Quantaco POC sync. Quick roll call — can you confirm?
00:05 Lena: Yep, Lena here. Good morning.
00:07 Markus: Markus here.
00:08 Priya: Priya—hi.
00:09 Ethan: Ethan from Redwood, ready to run through the numbers.
00:12 Sofia: Cool, agenda — bench recap, caching/kv cache results, batching tradeoffs, action items. Ethan you wanna start on the numbers?
00:20 Ethan: Yeah, quick reminder: last week we ran the 10k sample of your query set on r5-like instance with the 7B model variant, and we measured tokens/sec and cost per million tokens. Rough ballpark: with default settings we saw ~18k tokens/sec at about $0.12 per 1M tokens, that gives roughly 150k tokens per dollar over the run.
00:44 Lena: Wait, 18k tokens per second — is that steady state or peak?
00:49 Ethan: That was steady state during our 60s windows; peak was higher around 25k but the average across windows is ~18k. There's variance with long-tail requests.
00:59 Markus: How much is batch size influencing that? we saw weird latency jumps in our internal tests.
01:05 Ethan: Good call — batching is the single biggest lever for throughput. In our baseline we used dynamic batching with max batch 8. When we moved to max batch 16 throughput rose to ~26k tokens/sec, but p95 latency increased from 220ms to 480ms on the same GPU. So you trade latency for tokens/sec and therefore tokens per dollar.
01:32 Priya: So what does that mean for cost/unit? is it linear?
01:36 Ethan: Not linear. With batch16 you get roughly 1.45x better tokens per dollar because hardware utilization is higher, but tail latency and jitter go up. If your app can tolerate 300-500ms p95 it's a win. If you need strict sub-250ms p95 we recommend smaller batch or hybrid policy.
01:54 Avery: Are we including KV cache/prefix caching in those numbers?
01:58 Ethan: No, that's baseline. We ran a separate cache experiment — with prefix/KV cache warmed we saw a 28-33% reduction in consumed tokens for the dataset where a lot of prompts share prefixes. That maps directly to 28% lower cost for those traffic patterns. Important caveat: cache hit rate depends on request reuse; cold-starts won't help.
02:21 Lena: That 28% is promising. Our conversational flows have high prefix reuse on the product side so this could be bigger for us. But does caching change latency?
02:29 Ethan: Positive — cache hits reduce compute because KV cache avoids recomputing attention states, so p50 latency drops by ~15-20ms; p95 effect smaller but still positive. But cache invalidation and session sharding introduce complexity in a distributed setup.
02:44 Markus: Right we gotta think about session affinity and sticky routing for caching to be effective, otherwise we lose hits. Does Redwood provide sticky routing?
02:52 Sofia: Yes, we support affinity policies — you can route by session id to the same worker pool; Redwood's runtime also has automatic fallback if a node is down.
02:58 Markus: Ok good.
03:00 Priya: On the finance side I need to see projected dollars saved on our expected 10M monthly tokens baseline. Did you prepare a projection?
03:09 Ethan: We have a simple projection in the spreadsheet — with baseline (no cache, batch8) estimated cost is ~$1,200 per month for the sim traffic; with caching and batch16 it drops to about $820 — so roughly 30% savings in that scenario. Again depends on real traffic distribution.
03:28 Lena: Can we get that projection adjusted for mixed traffic — 60% short conv, 30% long generation, 10% embeddings?
03:35 Ethan: Yes we can — that's one of the things we'll update after we get the traces.
03:39 Sofia: Markus, can you confirm you'll send traces?
03:42 Markus: Yep, we'll scrub PII and send a 48h sample by Friday.
03:46 Ethan: Great — once we have traces we'll run a synthetic replay and show tokens/sec/$ by route.
03:55 Priya: One other question on model variants — you mentioned quantized 4-bit and fp16 options. How do those change cost/quality?
04:03 Ethan: Quantization usually reduces GPU memory and can increase throughput a bit; in our smoke runs Q4 reductions gave a 10-18% tokens/$ improvement with a small drop in generation quality for some of your longer instructions. FP16 is middle ground — small memory saving, small speed gains. The recommended approach is to run evals on your regen prompts to measure quality delta.
04:25 Lena: We do have a set of eval prompts for quality — Ethan can you run the quantized model against them and give quality/regression numbers?
04:33 Ethan: Yep, that's on the action list. We'll include BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and also human spot checks for hallucination rates.
04:41 Avery: Any security or deployment constraints that affect cost? for example if we need VPC or private deployment?
04:46 Sofia: Private deployment or VPC adds infra overhead; Dedicated reserved capacity has predictable throughput but higher baseline cost. If you go private, caching and batching still apply but your ops team manages the nodes. We can model both hosted and dedicated numbers in the spreadsheet.
05:03 Markus: For our compliance we need KMS integration and audit logs — do those add per-token costs?
05:09 Ethan: No per-token delta; encryption and audit logs are control-plane/ingest costs, small relative to inference. We'll add a line item for KMS/retention costs in the finance sheet.
05:18 Priya: Ok thanks. Can you summarize recommended config for our pilot to maximize savings without breaking SLAs?
05:25 Ethan: Sure: recommended starting point — use dynamic batching with max batch 8 for production latency-sensitive routes, enable KV prefix caching for conversational flows with sticky routing, run quantized model on non-critical long-generation routes, and reserve small burst capacity for peak windows. That gives good tokens/$ upside while keeping p95 mostly stable.
05:45 Lena: Sounds reasonable. How do we validate that caching doesn't change output semantics?
05:50 Ethan: Cache should be purely performance — it should not mutate outputs. We'll include regression checks in the eval harness to ensure identical outputs on cache hits versus cold runs. Small nondeterminism still possible; we'll log diffs.
06:06 Sofia: Quick check — timeline and next steps?
06:09 Ethan: I'll run the batch/quantization sweep and post results. Sofia will share cost sheet. Markus will send traces. Priya confirms budget. We'll reconvene next week same time for results review and then a security deep-dive mid-next week.
06:22 Priya: One procurement note — if we extend pilot we'll need a short contract amendment. I can prepare preliminary terms once we have numbers.
06:29 Sofia: Great. Any other questions?
06:33 Lena: Small nit — can you include per-route token distributions in the spreadsheet?
06:37 Sofia: Yes — we'll break down by route and by short/long/embedding buckets.
06:41 Ethan: Also we'll add a column for expected cache hit rate assumptions so you can tweak sensitivity.
06:46 Markus: For the batch experiments — can you also test tail latency percentiles (p99+p999) so we know worst-case?
06:53 Ethan: Yep, will include p50/p95/p99 and a p999 sample for the bigger batches.
06:59 Sofia: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the spreadsheet and schedule the security check.
07:05 All: Thanks, bye.

Recap / Notes:
- Baseline throughput ~18k tokens/sec, baseline cost ~ $0.12 per 1M tokens -> ~150k tokens per $1.
- Batch16 increases throughput to ~26k tokens/sec and gives ~1.45x tokens/$ improvement but increases p95 from ~220ms to ~480ms.
- KV/prefix cache can reduce token consumption by ~28-33% on traffic with high prefix reuse; improves p50 latency slightly. Cache effectiveness depends on sticky routing/session affinity.
- Quantization (Q4) estimated 10-18% tokens/$ improvement with potential small quality regressions; require eval.
- Private/Dedicated options change baseline costs; Redwood to model both in spreadsheet.

Artifacts to be shared: cost spreadsheet (redwood link), benchmark logs (s3/logs link), runbook for tuning (doc link).

End of transcript.
